findings.reason: §18 should collapse to a verification of an existing reader or delete, not a new implementation.
findings.text: §18's whole deliverable already exists: `gate_log_failure_ids` branches on `per_file_gate_runs` (review.py:2832) and returns the union of every marked file's failure ids, and it is documented as "the one reader both the review's added-failure count and the promotion-side readers go through" (promotion_checks.py:2448, promotion_evidence.py:1689, pending_landing.py:956). The test file `tests/test_a_per_file_gate_log_counts_every_failure.py:75` already asserts the exact case §18 lists first (three files, failures in the first two, union read), and its docstring names §18's incident verbatim: "the promotion's receipt reader once took the log's last run only ... refused a landing whose arm recorded six". A node briefed from §18 would rebuild a landed reader and re-add a passing test. The honest change, if anything remains, is to verify the landing path calls this reader rather than `last_run=True`.

findings.reason: §13's scope is either "route release through the existing declaration reader" or "extend its spellings", and those are different nodes.
findings.text: §13 proposes to make the release step tolerate a prose `commits` field, but `_commits_field_declares_absence` already parses a commitless role's field and its docstring names the three spellings §13 lists (`none.`, `none (review node)`, `none under the repository`), with `_commitless_raw_field` gating it on `_COMMITS_ROLES`. The brief for §13 must say whether the defect is that the *release* path (promotion_release.py) does not call this reader, or that the reader misses a fourth spelling — the plan text implies the former is unimplemented, which is not evident.

findings.reason: §2 should state whether it extends the forgotten-run derivation to session granularity or is a genuinely different fact; as written it re-derives.
findings.text: §2 derives "a session is lost" from follower liveness and unattended age, which `forgotten_runs` already derives: it reads `follower_registration._follower_liveness`, `runs._unattended_seconds`, and treats an unknown session as passed-threshold, with a documented threshold parameter. `session_host.live_census` (session_host.py:297) and `host_lease.process_runs_here` (host_lease.py:46) are the other two readers of the same three facts. A node briefed from §2 without this map will add a fourth read of the same state and a second threshold with the same meaning.

findings.reason: a second address field beside `transport` gives one row two addresses with no stated precedence.
findings.text: §11 adds a session address to the directory view, but the view already carries one: `_observed_transport` reads a `messaging_socket_path` from a run's stream and `_run_row` attaches it as `transport`, and `directory()` already aggregates them per coordinator as `coordinator["transports"]` (directory.py:804). The plan's "the name another session uses to message it" is a different address family (peer name from harness session files), which nothing under `reckon/` reads today — so the owner to extend is the transport resolution in `directory.py`, and the brief must say whether a peer name is a second address kind on the same field or a replacement.

findings.reason: "one test states that rule for both" is only honest if one function implements it for both.
findings.text: §10 says the git shim directory is "derived the same way" and should follow the scheduler shim rule, but `worker_shim_directory` (worker_git_shim.py:259) derives from `__file__` with no image rule at all, while `shim_directory` (nested_launch.py:452) carries the whole rule: `published_reload_image`, `SOURCE_ROOT_ENV`, `sys.prefix`'s parent, keep-own fallback. Implementing §10 by copying that block into `worker_git_shim.py` creates a second copy of a rule that must stay identical; the owner is `nested_launch.shim_directory`'s image-root resolution, which should be extracted to one function both callers pass their own directory name to.

findings.reason: the brief must name `readiness.py` as the owner, or the node forks the wait resolution.
findings.text: §5's `wait_class` classifies an awaiting-upstream request by what could release it, which is what `admission/readiness.py` already answers: `_wait_state` (readiness.py:770), `_ref_state` (readiness.py:1303), `wait_ref_kind` (readiness.py:448) and `dispatch_wait_blockers` (readiness.py:1080) resolve a wait's refs against the plan's declarations and the ledger. §5's three classes (progressing / idle / stranded) are a naming of the states that reader already computes, so the class belongs as an enum on `_wait_state`'s result, not as a parallel pass over the same refs. A second walk of `plan-section-depends-on` and the mount registry per request is the cost of not extending it.

findings.reason: the plan is right to describe endpoints only; this changes the brief, not the plan text.
findings.text: §2 (lost session), §5 (`wait_class`), §14 (live-with-no-process settled), §15 (head already landed) and §22 (landing-refused duty clears) each add a distinct predicate over the same live-pointer set, evaluated per pass per pointer, and each adds its own field to the directory row or obligations view. `classify_pointer` is the one module that already hides phase, classification and process liveness behind one call, and `_run_row` (directory.py:326) is the one place a row is built so "one run cannot read two ways across the views that render it". Five separate derivations instead of fields on that classification is the surface-spread this item is about: five passes over N pointers where one would do, and five chances for two views to disagree. The plan does not ask for the module, so this is a brief-level finding: the node composes them into the classifier's result.

findings.reason: the justification belongs in the node brief, which is where the item says it should go.
findings.text: §11 wraps `_observed_transport`'s result with a peer-name lookup and a boolean without saying why the existing `transport` cannot carry reachability (it already carries `observed_in`, a path into the stream it was read from, so liveness of that address is derivable). A wrapper that adds a name and a flag beside an address the row already holds is the parallel layer this item flags.

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds in its own text, per this item's rule.
findings.text: §2 adds three directory fields (`last_heard_at`, `lost`, `lost_since`) and a new flight setting `lost_session.after_hours`; §5 adds `wait_class` and `stranded_wait.report_after_hours`; §11 adds `peer_name` and `reachable`; §14 adds a settled phase and a setting; §19 adds a `stop-pending` phase; §24 adds a recorded command. That is six sections adding to the four counted families (public_definitions 3061, cli_options 528, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25) and not one states what it retires or merges. The obvious candidates the plan could name and does not: §2's three fields could replace `forgotten_runs`' separately-reported threshold, §5's class could subsume `WAIT_UNRESOLVABLE_PREFIX`'s scattered refusal strings, and §24's release command could merge with the existing resume-lane-change form §17 is repairing.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §2, §5, §14 and §15 each add a fresh derivation over the same live-pointer population where one classifier already answers for it, so the complexity lands in four readers instead of behind one.

rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 3061, cli_options 528, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; six sections add view fields, flight settings, a command or a phase and none names what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — four sections propose machinery that already exists at this revision: the per-file gate-log reader (§18), the commitless-commits declaration reader (§13), the shared-checkout shim-root rule (§10), and the session-loss derivation (§2, `forgotten_runs.py`).
